text.tspan: Long-running sagas · coordinated by the Message Broker
The two operations that change both player-db and game-db; chosen instead of two-phase commit (db-replication/README.md, "Sagas")
each call and after each answer
order, retried for up to 1 h
Each step is an ordinary gRPC call through the broker (breakers, load balancing and reroute apply)
and carries operation_id = saga:<id>:<step> (…:undo for a compensation), so a repeat changes nothing
THE TWO SAGAS · solid = steps in order, dashed red = compensation
takes min(40, xp) under a row lock
and answers how much was taken
if step 2 is refused or runs out of time
Before: game-service called player-service, then wrote its own
database. If that write failed, the XP was gone for good, and a
failed XP push at session end was only logged.
Now both changes happen, or the done ones are undone.
No lock is held across services while one of them is down,
which a two-phase commit would need.
forward recovery: retried until done, never undone
Isolation (sagas have none of their own)
• ENDING is a semantic lock: no new actions, steals or cycle ticks
• player-service decides 'taken' under SELECT … FOR UPDATE
• operation_id on every call: player XP ledger, game saga_operations
